newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Wave of prison riots continues in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Wave of prison riots continues in Colombia.

text.p: Another Colombian prison fell under the control of rebellious inmates on Tuesday -- the fourth since a wave of protests over poor living conditions and overcrowding erupted with the killing of four guards last week.

Police and penal authorities said the latest riot occurred in a penitentiary known as La Union in southwest Narino province where a group of more than 50 inmates was holding three guards hostage, demanding better treatment and the appointment of a new warden.

Some inmates hurled rocks and other debris at police and soldiers who cordoned off the facility after the riot erupted early on Tuesday, but there were no reports of serious violence or injuries, police said.

The situation was more volatile in Bucaramanga, capital of northern Santander province, where clashes erupted on Tuesday afternoon between inmates at the Modelo prison and police and soliders surrounding it since a riot started there on Monday.

Gunshots could be heard in radio reports from the scene and reporters said inmates armed with molotov cocktails and rocks were fighting pitched battles with security force members ringing the facility.
There were no immediate reports of injuries at Modelo, where authorities said the riot was staged to cover up an attempted mass breakout through a tunnel discovered by prison guards.

A tense standoff continued, meanwhile, at the main jail in Valledupar, capital of northern Cesar province, where an uprising by more than 580 prisoners has been under way since four guards were shot and killed inside the facility last Thursday.
Hundreds of security force members, backed by two light tanks, have ringed the prison -- which was built to hold no more than 150 inmates -- since the riot began.

Government officials have insisted that little progress can be made in the talks aimed at bringing the Valledupar uprising to a peaceful end unless the inmates, said to be led by a group of 10 men headed by a suspected leftist guerrilla, release 15 hostages and surrender the weapons they seized from prison guards.
At least 10 Colombian prisons have been torn by riots over the past two months but Thursday's bloodshed in Valledupar was the worst in recent memory.
A riot that erupted over the weekend at the Barne prison in central Tunja province ended peacefully on Monday.
Colombia's prison system was designed to hold a total of 30,000 inmates nationwide but authorities say 40,000 people are currently serving time behind bars.
